title: Administration Assistant
company: Clear Legal & Financial Recruitment - Agency - Permanent
description:
An excellent opportunity has arisen for an experienced Administration Assistant to join a busy professional services team in York.

This is a varied role where you will provide essential administrative, reception and office support, helping to ensure the smooth day-to-day running of the office. You will be a key point of contact for clients, visitors and colleagues, so a professional and approachable manner is essential.

The Role

Reporting to the HR & Office Manager, you will support the wider business with a range of administrative, reception and facilities responsibilities.

Reception & Administration

Act as the first point of contact for clients and visitors.
Manage a busy reception area and multi-line telephone system.
Manage the storage and retrieval of files, deeds and Wills, ensuring accurate records are maintained.
Record the removal and return of files, deeds and Wills.
Scan and archive closed files and maintain accurate records.
Carry out general administrative duties including photocopying, scanning and document distribution.
Monitor and respond to web enquiries.

Office & Facilities

Ensure reception equipment is operational and report any maintenance issues.
Order and maintain stationery and office consumables.
Arrange couriers and deliveries, including urgent collections and deliveries where required.
Obtain quotes and place orders for office furniture.
Assist with general office maintenance and report any defects.
Prepare meeting rooms and arrange refreshments and catering.
Carry out weekly fire alarm testing.

Financial & Compliance

Manage receipts for cash and cheque payments received at reception.
Handle petty cash and banking duties.
Process credit and debit card payments and complete end-of-day reports.
Distribute payment receipts to relevant colleagues.
Organise swears and take certified copies of identification documents.

Should you have any questions or wish to apply please do not hesitate to contact Clear Legal and Financial.

Please Note: Due to the number of applications we receive we may be unable to respond to every application directly.

title: Assistant Buyer/Purchasing Assistant
description:
Assistant Buyer - Construction

Location: York
Salary: 28,000- 33,000 + package
Job Type: Permanent

We are currently recruiting for an Assistant Buyer to join an established construction business and support the procurement team across a range of construction projects.

This is an excellent opportunity for an Assistant Buyer, Junior Buyer, Procurement Assistant or construction professional with some purchasing experience who is looking to develop their career within a busy commercial and procurement environment.

The Role

Working closely with the Buyer and wider commercial team, you will assist with the procurement of materials, subcontract packages and services, ensuring projects are delivered on time and within budget.

Key Responsibilities
- Assist with the procurement of materials, plant, subcontractors and specialist services.
- Obtain and compare quotations from suppliers and subcontractors.
- Prepare and issue enquiries and purchase orders.
- Assist with negotiating competitive prices and commercial terms.
- Maintain accurate procurement records and supplier information.
- Monitor orders and ensure materials and services are delivered in line with project requirements.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with suppliers and subcontractors.
- Assist with reviewing supplier and subcontractor performance.
- Support the Buyer and Quantity Surveying team with procurement activities.
- Monitor market prices and identify potential cost savings.
- Assist with managing procurement schedules and ensuring deadlines are achieved.
- Liaise with site teams, Quantity Surveyors, Estimators and Project Managers.
- Ensure procurement is carried out in accordance with company procedures and project requirements.

About You

The successful candidate will ideally have:
- Previous experience within construction procurement, buying or purchasing.
- Knowledge of construction materials, subcontract packages and supply chains.
- Strong communication and negotiation skills.
- Good commercial awareness and attention to detail.
- Excellent organisational and time-management skills.
- Good IT skills, particularly Microsoft Excel.
- The ability to manage multiple enquiries and deadlines.
- A proactive approach and willingness to develop within the role.

Candidates with experience as a Trainee Buyer, Junior Buyer, Procurement Assistant, Assistant Quantity Surveyor, Estimator or Commercial Assistant who are looking to move into construction procurement will also be considered.

Career Development

This role offers the opportunity to develop your procurement and commercial knowledge while working alongside experienced construction professionals, with clear potential to progress towards Buyer and Senior Buyer positions.

Apply today for more information and a confidential discussion about this opportunity.

title: Document Controller
description:
Document Controller

Nether Poppleton, York

Monday to Friday, Days

26 Days Holiday + Bank Holidays Company Pension Free Parking Development Opportunities

We are currently recruiting for a Document Controller to join a well-established and growing business within the construction industry.

This is a fantastic opportunity for an organised, detail-focused and proactive individual who is looking for a stable, long-term position where they can take ownership of document control and play an important role in the successful delivery of projects.

The position will involve managing and maintaining the flow of project documentation, ensuring information is accurate, up to date and compliant with both client and internal standards.

The Role

As the Document Controller, you will work closely with the wider project and office teams, taking responsibility for the organisation and control of important project documentation.

Responsibilities will include:
- Managing client document control systems
- Ensuring document updates and revisions are communicated to the relevant teams
- Maintaining accurate version control across project documentation
- Collating and compiling Operation & Maintenance (O&M) manuals
- Gathering information from suppliers and subcontractors
- Ensuring documents are correctly filed, maintained and easily retrievable
- Supporting multiple projects and working to deadlines
- Liaising with colleagues, clients, suppliers and subcontractors
- Providing additional office and administrative support when required
- Maintaining high standards of accuracy, organisation and communication

The position will involve working with document management platforms including 4 Projects, Aconex, Asite and SharePoint.

The Successful Candidate

We are looking for someone who is highly organised, professional and comfortable managing multiple priorities.

You will ideally have:
- Previous experience within document control, project administration or a similar role
- Experience using document management systems
- Experience with 4 Projects, Aconex, Asite and/or SharePoint
- Strong Microsoft Office skills, including Word, Excel and PowerPoint
- Excellent attention to detail
- Strong organisational and time-management skills
- Confident written and verbal communication
- The ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines
- A professional and customer-focused approach
- An interest in developing your knowledge of the construction industry

Experience within construction, engineering, roofing, cladding or a project-based environment would be particularly beneficial.

Due to the nature of some projects, the successful candidate will also be required to meet Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, including identity verification, employment history, criminal record and UK right-to-work checks.

Hours & Benefits

Monday to Thursday: 8:30am - 5:00pm, with a 1-hour lunch
Friday: 8:30am - 4:00pm, with a 1-hour lunch
Holiday: 26 days + Bank Holidays
Pension: Company pension scheme
Location: Nether Poppleton, York

title: HR Assistant
description:
Sewell Wallis are working with a well-regarded organisation who are now looking for an HR Assistant to join their HR team in York, North Yorkshire. This is a varied role where you'll have the opportunity to get involved across the full employee lifecycle and play an important part in delivering a professional HR service.

The role will see you working closely with the Head of HR, to provide day-to-day administrative support across recruitment, onboarding, employee relations, training, payroll and benefits, HR records and compliance.

You'll be a key point of contact for employees and managers, so being approachable, professional and comfortable dealing with confidential and sometimes sensitive situations is really important.

This would suit someone with strong HR experience who is looking for a role where they can broaden their knowledge, take on responsibility and develop their HR career.

What will you be doing?

Your responsibilities will include:
- Supporting employee relations processes, including disciplinary, grievance and capability procedures.
- Supporting managers with HR documentation, templates and general guidance.
- Helping with the end-to-end recruitment process, including drafting adverts, posting vacancies, screening applications and arranging interviews.
- Preparing new starter documentation, including offer letters, contracts and right to work checks.
- Coordinating inductions and probation reviews, keeping managers updated on progress and preparing confirmation or variation letters.
- Keeping employee records accurate and up to date across HR systems, including holiday, sickness and absence information and processing starters, leavers and contract changes in a timely manner.
- Responding to routine HR queries from employees and managers via email, telephone and internal systems.
- Coordinating internal training and e-learning, including booking venues, liaising with trainers and monitoring attendance.
- Supporting performance management and absence monitoring processes.
- You'll also have the opportunity to suggest improvements to HR processes and help the team make sure employees and managers receive a consistent, efficient and helpful service.

What skills are we looking for?

You'll ideally have:
- Around 4 years HR experience.
- Excellent organisational skills and a good eye for detail.
- The ability to manage multiple tasks and competing deadlines without losing track of the detail.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Word, Outlook and Excel.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- A professional, approachable and helpful manner.
- The ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with absolute discretion.
- Confidence communicating with employees, managers and external contacts.
- A proactive attitude and willingness to get stuck in.
- Good problem-solving skills and the confidence to ask questions when you're unsure.
- At least 2 GCSEs (or equivalent) at Grade A -C / 9-4, including English and Maths.
- If you're studying towards, or already hold, CIPD Level 3 that would be beneficial

What's on offer?

This is a fantastic opportunity to join an established HR team in a role where you'll get genuine exposure to a broad range of HR activity.
- Salary of between 28000 - 30000
- Above average holiday allowance
- Company pension scheme
- Company sick pay
- Cycle to work scheme
- Build a strong foundation for your longer-term HR career.

Send us your CV below, or contact Jemima Vibert for more information.

To apply please send your CV, quoting our reference and specifying which website you saw this position advertised on. Due to the high volume of applications please accept that if we have not responded to your application within seven days, your application has not been successful. We recruit at all levels within finance from Purchase Ledger Administrator and Credit Controller level through to Financial Controller and Director positions. With offices in Sheffield and Leeds, we are well situated to cover all of South Yorkshire, West Yorkshire and Manchester. title: Onboarding Administrator
description:
Sewell Wallis are excited to be working with a fantastic professional services business in York, North Yorkshire, who are looking for an Onboarding Administrator to join their Compliance team. This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys working in a busy environment, has excellent attention to detail and takes pride in delivering a really positive client experience.

You'll be the first point of contact for new clients, helping to make sure their onboarding journey is as smooth and straightforward as possible. You'll work closely with fee earners, support teams and colleagues across multiple offices, coordinating everything from initial documentation and compliance checks through to file closure.

What will you be doing?
- Acting as the main point of contact for new clients throughout the onboarding process.

- Coordinating the distribution, tracking and receipt of terms of business and other important client documentation.

- Supporting clients with forms and documentation, answering queries and providing a friendly, professional service throughout.
- Managing multiple onboarding cases at once, prioritising your workload and ensuring deadlines are met.
- Ensuring sensitive and confidential client information is handled securely and in line with relevant regulations.
- Coordinating file closures, making sure all documentation and compliance requirements are complete before files are archived.
- Supporting improvements to onboarding processes and helping to make the client journey as efficient as possible.

What are we looking for?

We're looking for someone who is organised, approachable and incredibly detail-focused, with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a busy environment.

You'll ideally have:
- Previous experience within a legal, compliance or professional services environment.
- Experience using case management or document management systems would be advantageous.
- Strong IT skills, including Microsoft Office.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- A professional and empathetic approach when dealing with clients and colleagues.
- Strong attention to detail and accurate data entry skills.
- Excellent organisation and time management skills.
- The ability to prioritise and manage your workload effectively.
- A proactive approach and willingness to get involved and support colleagues when needed.
- A minimum of 2 GCSEs at grade 4 or above (or equivalent), including English and Maths.

What's on offer?

title: Paralegal
company: LSL Property Services plc - Agency - Permanent
description:
LSL is a one of the largest providers of services to mortgage intermediaries, specialist mortgage and protection advice to estate agency and new build customers and valuation services to the UK's biggest mortgage lenders. It also operates a network of owned and franchised estate agency branches.

Based within our Group Legal Team in York, we are looking to recruit a Paralegal to provide support to the Group Legal Team with a wide variety of matters spanning across all areas of the LSL Group.

Location: York - on site office-based.

Role Purpose

To provide legal and administrative support to the Legal Team, assisting with a broad range of legal matters and ensuring the efficient delivery of legal services across the business. The role supports solicitors, contract administration, regulatory compliance, and corporate transactions whilst maintaining high standards of accuracy and professionalism.

Key Responsibilities
- Conduct legal research and prepare summaries, reports, and recommendations.
- Draft, review, and amend legal documents, including contracts, NDAs, agreements, and correspondence.
- Support solicitors and legal professionals on commercial, corporate, regulatory, and dispute resolution matters.
- Assist with contract management, document control, and legal record keeping.
- Monitor legal deadlines and maintain case and matter tracking systems.
- Prepare documentation for corporate transactions and business projects.
- Support regulatory and compliance activities.
- Liaise with internal stakeholders and external legal advisers where required.
- Assist with updating policies, procedures, and customer-facing terms and conditions.
- Ensure confidential information is handled appropriately at all times.

Knowledge, Skills & Experience
- Law degree, Legal Practice qualification, or equivalent legal education.
- Previous paralegal experience desirable but not essential.
- Strong legal research and analytical skills.
- Excellent written and verbal communication.
- High attention to detail and accuracy.
- Strong organisational and time-management abilities.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office and legal document management systems.
- Commercial awareness and understanding of legal risk.

Key Competencies
- Analytical thinking
- Attention to detail
- Professional integrity
- Communication and influencing
- Organisation and planning
- Problem solving
- Teamwork and collaboration
- Customer and stakeholder focus
